Market Intelligence Web Scraping

Automated collection of competitor and market data to feed pricing and demand models.

PythonWeb ScrapingMarket Intelligence

Overview

A companion piece to the Dynamic Pricing Optimizer, built during the same freelance engagement: the pricing model is only as good as the market data feeding it, so this project automated the collection of competitor prices and demand signals that had previously been gathered by hand.

Approach

A scheduled scraper walks a set of competitor listing pages, extracts price and availability, and normalizes everything into a shared schema regardless of which site it came from:

def scrape_listing(url, parser):
    """Fetch and normalize a single competitor listing."""
    response = fetch_with_backoff(url)
    raw = parser.extract(response.text)
    return {
        "sku": normalize_sku(raw["sku"]),
        "price": parse_price(raw["price"]),
        "in_stock": raw["availability"] == "available",
        "scraped_at": now_utc(),
    }

Retry-with-backoff and per-domain rate limiting kept the scraper polite and stable against sites that rotated their markup periodically — a per-site parser adapter meant a markup change only broke one adapter, not the whole pipeline.

Result

Feeding fresher, more complete competitor data into the pricing model was a direct input into the 30% efficiency gain described in the pricing optimizer write-up — stale market data had been causing the model to misprice against competitors who’d already moved.
